issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and introduction say that the result (a unique HM for each degree and boundary condition) is extended to p.c.f. fractals, and that the method applies to that large class. Theorem thm.pcf asserts only existence. It also relies on postulated, unverified properties of cycle embeddings and cut points, which are absent from its statement and are illustrated only by figures. The Discussion concedes that uniqueness is not claimed, yet it asserts uniqueness 'by construction' within a homotopy class. That assertion has no support: there is no homotopy classification for p.c.f. sets (no analog of thm.homotopy) and no uniqueness argument.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, we extend this result to HMs on p.c.f. fractals.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the p.c.f. contribution as existence under explicit hypotheses \eqref{cycle_extend}-\eqref{pcf-cut}. Remove the uniqueness claims, or supply a homotopy classification and a uniqueness proof.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised generalization of Strichartz's theorem, and the conjecture it is said to settle, are not established for p.c.f. fractals. Only conditional existence is stated.
issues.title: Abstract/introduction claim the uniqueness theorem is extended to p.c.f. fractals
issues.why_classification: An advertised extension (uniqueness, full p.c.f. scope) must be withdrawn or conditioned. The existence result itself survives in comparable form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The key point is to check that $F$ is well defined as a continuous map from

issues.failure_explanation: For T-valued f and g, the expression tf+(1-t)g mod 1 depends on the chosen real representatives, so F is not defined pointwise. The proof checks closure along each loop separately, implicitly using lifts along that loop. Loops in P share vertices and edges, however, and a consistent global choice of lifts requires lifting f-g to a real continuous function on G. That step needs the vanishing of all degrees of f-g together with a cycle-basis/lifting argument, and the proof never gives it; the hypothesis (for-all-gamma) is not even used explicitly. The claimed uniform continuity on P×[0,1] is asserted without argument.

failure_location.quote: Thus, $F$ is a uniformly continuous function on $\mathcal{P}\times [0,1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a lifting lemma. If all degrees of h=f-g vanish, then h has a continuous real lift on G: lift on each Γ_n using that P-loops of level ≤n form a cycle basis, show uniform continuity from small oscillation on small cells, and extend by density. Then use F=g+t·lift(h).
issues.overall_effect: The 'if' direction (equal degree vectors imply homotopic maps) is unproved. So is the stated interpretation that HMs represent homotopy classes.
issues.title: Straight-line homotopy of T-valued maps is ill-defined; the loop-by-loop check does not give a global homotopy
issues.why_classification: The statement survives, but a contained new lifting argument replaces the invalid one.

Intuitively, it is clear that $\hat f^\ast:\, G\to \T$ is the desired HM.

issues.failure_explanation: The Laplacian of a T-valued map, and hence 'HM', is never defined. The only uniqueness argument is in Section 6, and it fails on four counts. (i) The energy identity is shown only for $\hat f^*$. Comparing with a competitor g needs a lift of g to the covering space, and no lifting lemma is given. (ii) $\hat H$ fixes only δ1, δ2 and ρ0, not the degree vector (homotopy-c), so it mixes homotopy classes. Minimizing over it cannot single out the HM of a prescribed class; the paper itself asserts that HMs exist in every class. (iii) Monotonicity of $\hat\cE_m$ for arbitrary T-valued maps is deduced from (E-extension), which concerns real lifted functions. (iv) As written, (Em-hat) uses unsquared d_T and the threshold π instead of 1/2, so the claimed identity with $E[\Gamma_m^0]$ fails.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In addition, for every $1\le m\le N$ and $w\in S^m$.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\mathbf f(x,k)=f(x)+k$ and f(c_+)=f(c_-)+ρ, consistency requires gluing c_+^k to c_-^{k+ρ}. (eq:sg_gen_cuts) glues c_-^k to c_+^{k+ℓ(w)}, which is the reversed direction and shifts by the index ℓ(w) instead of ρ_{ℓ(w)}. For γ_0, Section 7 and the Appendix glue z_-^k to z_+^{k+ρ0}, giving a mismatch of 2ρ0. The Appendix also lists cuts only for 1≤m≤N, so the level-1 cells, with degrees ρ1–ρ3, receive no cuts.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Glue c_+^k to c_-^{k+ρ_{ℓ(w)}} uniformly, including γ_0, and run the Appendix over 0≤m≤N-1.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the covering space for higher-order degrees does not carry a well-defined lift realizing the prescribed degree vector.
issues.title: Higher-order cut identifications inconsistent with the jump conditions
issues.why_classification: The consistent correction is forced by H_m^k, and the construction and claims survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $K$ is called a p.c.f. fractal if $V_0$ is finite.

issues.failure_explanation: F_w^{-1} is the full inverse of a bijection of R^d. For SG with y=(v2+v3)/2 ∈ C, the points F_{1^n}^{-1}(y)=2^n(y-v1)+v1 are distinct for every n. So V_0 is infinite, SG is not p.c.f. under this definition, and the intended V_0={v1,v2,v3} is not recovered.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the standard post-critical set, e.g. F_w^{-1}(C∩K_w), or the code-space definition.
issues.overall_effect: The class to which Theorem thm.pcf applies is mis-specified and excludes SG and the paper's examples.
issues.title: Definition of the post-critical set V_0 makes SG non-p.c.f.
issues.why_classification: A standard local correction restores the intended class.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) Edges of Γ_m are defined only by c^m_xy>0 and need not be paths in K. Hence 'the corresponding loop', the degrees ω_γ, and ρ0=ω_p(f) are undefined, and ρ0 is in any case determined by the ρ_i because γ0∈Cyc(Γ_m). (ii) The fundamental-domain conditions f(v_i)-f(v_{i-1})=δ_{i-1} equal the lifted increments in (pcf-bc-hm) only if no cut point lies on the γ0-arc between them. Nothing in (cycle_extend)-(pcf-cut) excludes cut points of basis cycles that share edges with γ0. (iii) H_m^k consists of functions on V_m, yet imposes jumps at points of V_{m+1}. Harmonicity at the glued cut points, with several cuts and general conductances, is asserted 'as in' the SG two-sheet argument but never verified.
